_description: The Earth surface tier table — GENERATED by tools/pipeline/build-earth-tiers.js --write (plan 27 step E). The scene picks the day map by the TT age of its epoch from `tiers` (ages in Myr before J2000; each tier cross-fades to the next younger tier's map over `fadeMyr` at its younger edge; `clouds` and `atmosphere` scale the cloud shell and the blue atmosphere shell, both 0 over the magma ocean). `kind` names what a map IS: cited paleogeography (Scotese 2016, CC BY 4.0) or generated illustration (the model does not model continents). The gate tools/verify/earth-tiers.js checks the files against `files`.

scotese2016.title: PALEOMAP PaleoAtlas for GPlates and the PaleoData Plotter Program (PaleoAtlas v3 rasters)
scotese2016.citation: Scotese, C.R., 2016. PALEOMAP PaleoAtlas for GPlates and the PaleoData Plotter Program, PALEOMAP Project. Distributed in the Zenodo record of Scotese, C.R. & Wright, N., 2018, PALEOMAP Paleodigital Elevation Models (PaleoDEMS) for the Phanerozoic.
scotese2016.preparation: the bottom-left file-name label replaced by the 31x31 median of its 230x34 box; the present-day coastlines and political boundaries the originals draw in black ink over every reconstruction REMOVED and filled from their surroundings (tools/pipeline/lib/remove-drawn-lines.js: thin features at most 0.45 of their local background's luminance, in connected pieces of at least 24 px, 1–3 % of a map, and the fainter US state grid as long thin pieces at most 0.65 of the background — a change to the licensed work, stated here as CC BY 4.0 requires; a few fragments over the darkest sea and some short island outlines stay in); rolled by 180° to the scene's Pacific-centred seam; Lanczos resize to 2048 x 1024; WebP quality 85.

generated.note: procedural illustration rendered by this script from seeded 3-D value noise on the sphere (seed 20261103; the recipes' parameters are in the script) — no third-party rights; labelled "illustration" on every surface

derived.note: the present-day map with its vegetation desaturated to an ochre desert (the biosphere's end), and that under a seeded vapour deck with the seas darkened (the moist greenhouse) — derivatives of the CC BY 4.0 map, labelled "illustration"; the spans a reading of the literature below

literature.caldeiraKasting1992: Caldeira, K. & Kasting, J.F., 1992. The life span of the biosphere revisited. Nature 360, 721–723 — C₃ photosynthesis ends at ~+0.5–0.9 Gyr as CO₂ is drawn down under the brightening Sun.
literature.franck2006: Franck, S., Bounama, C. & von Bloh, W., 2006. Causes and timing of future biosphere extinctions. Biogeosciences 3, 85–92 — the land biosphere ends ~+0.8–1.2 Gyr.
literature.leconte2013: Leconte, J., Forget, F., Charnay, B., Wordsworth, R. & Pottier, A., 2013. Increased insolation threshold for runaway greenhouse processes on Earth-like planets. Nature 504, 268–271 — the runaway at ~+1 Gyr.
literature.wolfToon2015: Wolf, E.T. & Toon, O.B., 2015. The evolution of habitable climates under the brightening Sun. JGR Atmospheres 120, 5775–5794 — the moist greenhouse sets in at ~+1 Gyr.
literature.zahnle2007: Zahnle, K., Arndt, N., Cockell, C., Halliday, A., Nisbet, E., Selsis, F. & Sleep, N.H., 2007. Emergence of a habitable planet. Space Science Reviews 129, 35–78 — the rock-vapour and steam atmospheres after the impact, the rain-out.
literature.hamano2013: Hamano, K., Abe, Y. & Genda, H., 2013. Emergence of two types of terrestrial planet on solidification of magma ocean. Nature 497, 607–610 — the magma ocean crystallises in 1–4 Myr at 1 AU.
literature.sleep2001: Sleep, N.H., Zahnle, K. & Neuhoff, P.S., 2001. Initiation of clement surface conditions on the earliest Earth. PNAS 98, 3666–3672 — clement conditions within ~10 Myr of the impact.
literature.wilde2001: Wilde, S.A., Valley, J.W., Peck, W.H. & Graham, C.M., 2001. Evidence from detrital zircons for the existence of continental crust and oceans on the Earth 4.4 Gyr ago. Nature 409, 175–178 — liquid water by 4,400 Ma.
literature.zahnle2006: Zahnle, K., Claire, M. & Catling, D., 2006. The loss of mass-independent fractionation in sulfur due to a Palaeoproterozoic collapse of atmospheric methane. Geobiology 4, 271–283 — the Archean methane haze.
literature.arney2016: Arney, G. et al., 2016. The pale orange dot: the spectrum and habitability of hazy Archean Earth. Astrobiology 16, 873–899 — the orange organic haze.

tiers.label: The moist greenhouse — the oceans evaporating under a brightening Sun, a reading of Leconte 2013 and Wolf & Toon 2015 (derived)
The end of the land biosphere — CO₂ starvation of the plants under a brightening Sun, a reading of Caldeira & Kasting 1992 and Franck 2006 (derived)
